newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: Aegon '96 profit seen over 17 pct higher.
newsitem.headline: Aegon '96 profit seen over 17 pct higher.

text.p: Dutch insurer Aegon, with its focus on life insurance, is expected to announce a 1996 net profit rise of just over 17 percent to some 1.55 billion guilders on Friday, analysts said.
Analysts' forecasts varied little, ranging between 1.54 billion and 1.57 billion guilders.

They said life insurance in its home base and the United States was growing rapidly, while non-life results had recovered and the relatively small banking activities were also expected to be substantially higher.
Analysts forecast a profit rise of 18.6 percent to 451 million guilders for the final quarter of 1996, which would be the strongest increase for the year.
Results rose 12.6 percent in the first quarter of 1996, 15.7 percent in the first six months and 16.6 percent in the first nine months.
They expect the 1996 dividend to rise to 2.75 guilders per share from 2.37 guilders in 1995.
Analyst Bart van der Feen of Rabo Securities forecast that Aegon would post a net profit of 1.55 billion guilders in 1996 and was also upbeat on the years to come.
"Growth continues and we foresee earnings per share and dividend rising 13.5 percent in the years ahead," he said.
"About 10 percent of Aegon's growth will be related to organic growth and the remainder to acquisitions and expansion in new markets."
Aegon is expanding gradually in Asia and has said it is still interested in expanding into Scandinavia after it failed to acquire Norwegian life insurer Vital in 1995.
Analyst Hans Pluygers of Kempen said Aegon might also widen its focus and start business in Brazil since it was already operating in Mexico.
Pluygers did not exclude a share split for Aegon since the stock has risen substantially to 135 guilders per share from some 100 guilders at the end of 1996.
"Aegon shares have risen above 120 guilders, which could be a signal for a share split," said Van der Feen.
But he added Aegon might also wait until the intended acquisition of U.S. Providian, which was announced on December 30, 1996 was finalised.
He said a share split could wait until the deal was done.
